# dsh-websearch-keyless
**Make DeepSeek Harness's native `web_search` work with no API key at all.**

Mirrors the three keyless search backends that OpenCode's `WebSearch` service ships with —
Tavily, T
inyFish and Exa — and registers them as a `ctx.web` search provider.
English | 简体中文
## The problem

A DSH profile with no usable search provider falls back on
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-search-deepseek`, w

hich answers `web_search` through the DeepSeek **chat**
API. When that key is missing or invalid, ev

_search` through the DeepSeek **chat**
API. When that key is missing or invalid, every search fails:

## The fix

OpenCode's `WebSearch` service registers five providers; three of them run keyless. This plugin
mirr

ors those three, in priority order, falling through to the next when one fails, times out, or
return

three, in priority order, falling through to the next when one fails, times out, or
returns nothing:
| Order | Backend | Endpoint | Keyless signal |

| 1 | Tavily | `POST https://api.tavily.com/search` | `X-Tavily-Access-Mode: keyless` |
| 2 | TinyFi

sh | `POST https://agent.tinyfish.ai/mcp` | `X-TinyFish-Access-Mode: keyless` |
| 3 | Exa | `POST ht
tps://mcp.exa.ai/mcp` | no key parameter |

No signup, no key, no config. Only `web_search` is taken over — `web_fetch` keeps using the
built-in

built-in HTTP provider.
### How this differs from other keyless DSH search plugins

There are several keyless plugins for DSH now. Some read public search endpoints directly (for
examp

le DuckDuckGo HTML or Bing), which works, but tends to return thin snippets with no
first-party meta

ckDuckGo HTML or Bing), which works, but tends to return thin snippets with no
first-party metadata.
This one calls the same first-party search APIs that OpenCode uses, in keyless mode:

- real titles and body snippets rather than scraped result markup
- three independent providers, so

one being throttled does not take search down
- two source files, zero dependencies, no build step,
no DSH peer dependencies

## How it works

The registered provider implements the seam's interface verbatim:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`available()` returns `true` unconditionally because none of the backends need credentials.
Failures

map onto the seam's codes: `WEB_ABORTED` for cancellation, `WEB_PROVIDER_ERROR` when
every backend
fails for a reason rather than legitimately returning nothing.
### Compatibility

Tested against **DSH 0.2.1-rc.3**. The plugin declares **no `@deepseek-ai/*` peer dependencies and
n

o `engines.dsh`**, deliberately — DSH runs `evaluatePluginCompatibility` against every manifest
befo

re loading it, so declaring nothing means nothing can be unmet. It also uses no
`@deepseek-ai/*` imp
orts, so it resolves with a plain `link:` and needs no build step.
## Gotchas

These three cost real debugging time. If you write your own DSH web provider, they will bite you

**1. `fetchProvider` must be restated.** An id-targeted patch entry **replaces** the matched
plugin'

s `config` object; it does not deep-merge. The shipped default lives in
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`'s

layer as `{ searchProvider: deepseek-official, fetchProvider: http }`.
Override only `searchProvide

r` and `fetchProvider` is silently dropped — every `web_fetch` then
fails with:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

**2. A `[]` sentinel breaks appends.** A profile with no overrides yet has a literal `[]` as its
ent
ire `cordis.patch.yml`. Appending blocks after it creates a second YAML document:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Remove the `[]` first.

**3. Do not add DSH peer dependencies.** Any `@deepseek-ai/*` peer range that does not cover the
run
ning version gets the plugin skipped at boot:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
If you must load a plugin whose ranges are stale, grant an exact-version exemption:

| Symptom | Cause |
| `WEB_PROVIDER_CONFIGURED_MISSING` | `searchProvider: opencode-keyless` is set but the plugin did n
ot load — check the plugin is in `dependencies` **and** `bundles`, and that `node_modules/dsh-websea

rch-keyless` resolves |
| `multiple usable web providers are registered` | Gotcha 1 — add `fetchProv

ider: http` |
